clue.text: Intrusions caused by old-fashioned inside lock

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, so the word for lock is opened to take the word for old-fashioned

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
passé means out of date, old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Someone complains of intrusions brought on by an outdated lock that no longer keeps people out.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespasses are unlawful entries onto another's land, a plain synonym for intrusions.

clue.text: Guess southern Germany in part should turn to north

indicators.note: one letter should become another, so the lower D of the word for part is swapped for N

parts.note: to part is to divide
D is the international code for Germany; southern means the lower one in this down entry

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders whether part of southern Germany should head north.
explanation.walkthrough: DIVIDE has two Ds; in a down entry the 'southern' one is the lower, the last D, which becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to discover by intuition, so it is a synonym for guess.

clue.text: Low offer to pen opener for rock singer

parts.note: feeling low is feeling blue

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the word for offer holds the next letter

parts.note: a bid is an offer at auction

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rock singer is made a disappointing offer to sign up as an opening act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock singer' looks like one phrase, but 'rock' only supplies R; the definition is 'singer'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebird is a North American songbird, so it is a kind of singer.

clue.text: Miss stops recording exclusive

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so the word for miss plugs the recording

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc recording
to miss a chance is to lose it

explanation.surface: A newsroom misses its exclusive because recording stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed club or meeting is exclusive, open only to a chosen few.

clue.text: Female with account in excellent company set up to supply bread

indicators.note: the account abbreviation goes in the middle of the reversed pair
in a down entry, set up means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI

explanation.surface: A woman with an account at a fine firm is set up to supply bread to it.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, written AI, is old slang for first-rate; 'set up' reads upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Focaccia is a flat Italian loaf flavoured with olive oil, a kind of bread.

clue.text: Attend strike repeatedly

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ..., meaning attend or be present at

explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'be at' it means attend; as one word, beat means hitting repeatedly, as on a drum.

clue.text: Guy picked up fish drink

parts.note: a guy is a tent rope, a cord

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: an eel is a fish; said after cord it gives the end of the drink's sound

explanation.surface: A man hooks a fish and has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is not a man but a tent rope, CORD; CORD EEL said aloud is CORDIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial is a sweet fruit-flavoured concentrate diluted to make a drink.

clue.text: Horror story and awful gripe about messenger

parts.note: Carrie is Stephen King's horror novel

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of gripe are in a terrible mess

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone combines a horror tale with a nasty complaint about a messenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges GRIPE to RPIGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier pigeon is a homing bird trained to fly messages, so it is a messenger.

clue.text: US lawman has given name to uncover predator

indicators.note: uncovering a word strips its outer letters, its first and last

parts.note: Eliot was the first name of the US lawman Eliot Ness
Eliot Ness was the US Prohibition agent who pursued Al Capone

explanation.surface: An American lawman and his first name are set to expose a predatory criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The given name is that of the lawman himself, ELIOT, with its ends removed to give LIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is the female lion, the main hunter of the pride, so a predator.

clue.text: Kept an eye on lovely fiance

parts.note: super means lovely, splendid
one's intended is one's fiancé

explanation.surface: A woman watched over her lovely fiancé.
explanation.definitionFit: To superintend is to supervise, so superintended means watched over or supervised.

clue.text: Loyalty overlooking leader's worn condition

indicators.note: to overlook the leader is to leave out the first letter

parts.note: trustiness is faithfulness, loyalty

explanation.surface: Loyalty to a leader is said to overlook how worn out that leader is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's worn' reads as one phrase, but the possessive belongs to the indicator; the definition is 'worn condition'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustiness is the state of being corroded or out of practice, a worn state.

clue.text: Clone marred with this malfunction might be conceptual

indicators.note: something marred is spoiled, so the letters are jumbled together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sci-fi idea: a clone spoiled by a glitch might be a mere concept.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CLONE plus the answer, jumbled, spell CONCEPTUAL; 'this' stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to behave badly or fail to work properly, as a machine does.

clue.text: Foolish king Danes totally unmasked

indicators.note: unmasking each word takes off its outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A foolish Viking king exposes his Danes completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totally' means both words lose their ends: IN from KING, ANE from DANES.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and lacking sense, a synonym for foolish.

clue.text: Mark in register police group reviewed

indicators.note: re-viewed suggests looking again from the other end, so read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a register of duties
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the police

explanation.surface: A mark is entered in the register when a police unit is inspected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' turns ROTACID into DICATOR, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicator is a sign or pointer, and a mark is likewise a sign showing something.

clue.text: Equal beat at climbing tor

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, a mount

explanation.surface: Climbing a tor is said to be equal to a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns AT into TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantamount to means equivalent in effect to, so it means equal.

clue.text: Continued deliberate backtracking inflamed hosts

indicators.note: to host is to hold within, so the outer word takes in the other

parts.note: inflamed skin is red

indicators.note: backtracking means going back, read in reverse

parts.note: to muse is to ponder, deliberate

explanation.surface: Talks resumed after the inflamed delegates backtracked on a deliberate plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracking' turns MUSE into ESUM, which RED hosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Resumed means carried on after a pause, so continued.

clue.text: US city regularly ignored their tin shelters

indicators.note: to shelter is to hold within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: tin is slang for money

indicators.note: every other letter is ignored, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: In some American city they routinely overlook their tin shacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin' is not the metal but old slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Monterey is a coastal city in California, so a city in the US.

clue.text: River in south drained in the year, before November

indicators.note: the year comes first, before the November letter
a drained word has its contents emptied, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: anno is Latin for 'in the year', as in anno Domini
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A river in the south was drained during the year, before November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained' empties SOUTH to SH. The Shannon is Ireland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland and the British Isles.

clue.text: Drawn theatrical act out after late tackle's deployed

indicators.note: out means taken away, so these letters leave the pool
deployed means arranged differently, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: a theatrical act is simply an act on stage

explanation.surface: A drawn-out theatrical performance follows a late tackle in a sporting match.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ACT from LATE TACKLES and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn means haggard and gaunt, and skeletal means so thin the bones show.

clue.text: Suggest reform of United Nations? Don't fancy being dismissed

indicators.note: a reform reshapes, so the letters are rearranged
fancy suggests ornamental rearrangement of the removed letters
dismissed means sent away, so these letters leave the pool

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hints at reform of the United Nations, but dislikes the idea of being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange UNITED NATIONS without the letters of DON'T.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to hint or imply indirectly, so it means to suggest.

clue.text: A command for dogs to bite bishop is surprise

indicators.note: the outer word bites, holding the other in its teeth

parts.note: mush is the musher's call to sled dogs
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A sled-dog command makes the dogs bite a bishop by surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a surprise attack from a hidden position.

clue.text: Eating third of vindaloo, cause wind

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: sake is a cause, as in 'for the sake of'

indicators.note: the third letter of the word

explanation.surface: Eating vindaloo can cause wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' is not flatulence but the verb to wind, to twist and turn; N goes inside SAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake is to wind along a twisting course, like a road through hills.

clue.text: Heartlessly swap present for compass

indicators.note: without its heart, a word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone callously swaps a present for a compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compass' is not the instrument but range or scope.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass means scope or range, as does sphere, a field of action or influence.

clue.text: Destroy base after ages

indicators.note: the base letter follows the ages word

parts.note: eras are ages, long periods
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A military base is destroyed after ages of service.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or obliterate, so to destroy.

clue.text: Last of many to raise voice

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for many is the one that moves
in a down entry, raising a letter moves it higher, earlier in the word

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: The last of many people stand up to make their voice heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The final T of ALOT moves up one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a singing voice, the lowest female or highest adult male range.

clue.text: Audibly sands court door, primarily timber

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is spoken and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a beach is sands
to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: primarily means first, the first letter

explanation.surface: A carpenter sands a courtroom door, which is chiefly timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sands' is a noun, the beach, not a verb about sanding wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Beechwood is the wood of the beech tree, a timber for furniture.

clue.text: Kernels covering stone in floor, all around

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the whole is reversed
the stone word goes in the floor word

parts.note: to floor someone is to stun them
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: Seeds coat a stone set into a floor all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' is the verb, to knock someone down, not the surface underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmegs are the hard aromatic seeds of a tropical tree, kernels used as spice.

clue.text: Article for study returned in protective cover

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: returned means sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room

explanation.surface: A paper submitted for a study comes back in a protective sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns DEN into NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Aproned means wearing an apron, a garment covering clothes to protect them.
